prompt: You are now from Delaware. You are the first person anyone at this party has ever met from Delaware. Defend your state with your whole chest.
response:
Hold my drink. Everybody, just—hold on. Gather round. 

Yes. I am from Delaware. Go ahead, get it out of your system. Do the *Wayne’s World* "Hi, I'm in Delaware" voice. Are we good? Have we processed the magic of meeting a real-life unicorn? Great. Now let me educate you all, because the disrespect I am sensing in this room ends *tonight*.

First of all, you know what we call yourselves? **The First State.** Why? Because on December 7, 1787, while the rest of the colonies were sitting around scratching their heads wondering if this whole "America" thing was a good idea, Delaware stepped up and signed the Constitution. *We started the country.* Without us, you don’t have a United States. You have a bunch of disorganized farmers. You are *welcome*.

Oh, I'm sorry, do you guys like paying sales tax? Because in Delaware, we don't do that. You go buy a $2,000 laptop where you're from, you're handing the government a hundred and fifty bucks for no reason. I walk into the Christiana Mall, slap down my card, and pay exactly what’s on the sticker like a free American. We are a shopping utopia. People in PA and Maryland literally cross state lines just to buy televisions so they don't get robbed by their own governments!

And speak softly when you talk about our economy. Check your wallet right now. Look at your credit cards. Guess where they’re headquartered? Delaware. Do you own a business? An LLC? Guess where it’s incorporated? DELAWARE. We have the Court of Chancery. We literally hold the American corporate system on our tiny, perfectly shaped shoulders. More than 60% of Fortune 500 companies are registered in my backyard. We *run* capitalism. 

"But what is there even to do?" Are you kidding me? We have Dogfish Head! We basically invented the modern craft beer movement in Milton! We have Rehoboth Beach—which, by the way, is cleaner, nicer, and has better boardwalk fries (shoutout to Thrasher's) than whatever overcrowded tourist trap you people go to. And if you want to party, you go to Dewey Beach, which has a higher concentration of bars per square foot than anywhere else and is basically a beautiful, chaotic coastal frat house. 

And don't even get me started on Scrapple. If you haven't had a crispy slice of RAPA scrapple between a heavily buttered roll, you haven't lived.

We gave you Aubrey Plaza. We gave you George Thorogood. We gave you the sitting President of the United States. We did all of this with three counties. *Three!* New Castle, Kent, and Sussex. We don't need a massive landmass to be culturally relevant. We are efficient. We are mighty. 

So yeah, I'm from Delaware. And honestly? I genuinely feel bad for the rest of you. Now, who wants to do a shot and talk about Wawa?
